text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Details about shortages in Swedish schools are laid out in a secret report received by the paper. Schools Minister Ylva Johansson says she wants to give more money to the education system.

- Swedish fashion designer, Richard Bengtsson, who formerly worked for Hennes & Mauritz in Sweden, is making a name for himself and his partner Edward Pawlichs in New York. The pair have a design studio in SoHo and have won an award as best new comers in the industry.
- The new head of the Swedish National Economic Research Institue, KI, Svante Oberg, 50, says he wants to build up international contacts and create new opportunities.
- More demand for environmentally friendly paper should be created, an environment group said.

- At least 50 new companies are on their way to the Stockholm bourse with at least half of these expected to list this year. Computer and drug companies dominate the list and are battling to get risk capital.
- A newspaper survey finds that Banco Fonders' managing director Kajsa Lindstahl is the highest paid leader in funds receiving over three million crowns in her pay packet alone.

- Prime Minister Goran Persson says that Sweden has a good climate for companies. He says smaller companies are very important to increase the number of jobs in the private sector and this is the reasoning behind putting an extra 10 billion crowns to commuity use.
